newsitem.title: INDIA: CRICKET-ASTLE SHINES BUT NEW ZEALAND STILL STRUGGLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ASTLE SHINES BUT NEW ZEALAND STILL STRUGGLE.

text.p: New Zealand struggled to
220 for nine in their Independence Cup match against India on
Wednesday despite another fine innings by opener Nathan Astle
who narrowly missed a second successive century.
Astle and Bryan Young gave New Zealand a brisk start by
putting on 59 for the first wicket but the scoring rate slowed
later in the innings and they lost four wickets through run
outs.
Astle hit 10 boundaries, including three in one over off
medium-pacer Abey Kuruvilla, and was particularly severe on the
off-side as he scored 92 from 111 balls. It followed his 117
against Pakistan at Mohali in the opening match of the
tournament last Friday.
The opener, who survived a difficult chance at mid-off when
he was on 52, was eventually bowled by seamer Robin Singh.
Sunil Joshi, who dismissed Young for 17 and took two for 47,
also figured in two successive run outs as the New Zealand
batting faltered.
Matthew Horne (23), who added 50 with Astle for the second
wicket, was run out by a quick throw from Joshi at square-leg
while captain Stephen Fleming (13) was Joshi's second run out
victim as he hesitated after hitting Singh to mid-wicket.
Singh then trapped Chris Cairns lbw for three before
dismissing Astle soon after.
Adam Parore tried to increase the tempo and scored 32 from
53 balls before he was also run out in the last over to a direct
hit by skipper Sachin Tendulkar.
